Write authorization-inquiry/v1 from this CURRENT natural brief. Do not answer the source question, infer code behavior, add an expectation, future policy or unprovided premises.
Fields: schemaVersion, mode behavior|conformance, questions:[{id,request,principal?,resource?,operation?,entryHint?,premises:[{text,origin:user}]}], optional policy:{text,origin:user|external-policy,location} only for conformance.
Keep every requested scenario in question.request or a separate question. Optional principal/resource/operation are task wording, never invented code facts. Unspecified facts remain unspecified. Conformance copies the independently supplied policy verbatim.
Unrelated synthetic example: {schemaVersion:'authorization-inquiry/v1',mode:'behavior',questions:[{id:'museum',request:'Can a visitor reserve an exhibit?',premises:[]}]}. This is a structural example with no source answer.

Current mode: behavior
Current user policy: null
Current natural brief:
Declare only the current user question, never a source answer.

The actual runtime supplies the current mode and independent policy. For conformance copy that policy exactly. Compile once using authorization_compile({inquiry}). Read source through source_list/search/symbol/read. Propose local changes with authorization_observe({controlDelta}); optional observations are {questionId,kind,subject,object?,claim,state,evidenceIds}. All source citations must already be shown.

domain-evidence-v1 runtime: propose local control deltas from ACTUALLY SHOWN original source, never from task expectations. Host binds citations, executes at most two uniquely located dependency reads per response, evaluates finite predicates and checks formal conclusion consistency. Extraction meaning stays unreviewed.
Delta is {schemaVersion:"authorization-control-slice/v1",rules:[],dependencies:[],bindings:[],policyRules:[]}. Arrays may be omitted when unchanged. Local rules: {key,questionId,pathKey,kind:entry|binding|guard|reject|continue|effect,after:[predecessor keys],evidenceIds:[shown source IDs],claim,condition?,principal?,resource?,operation?,bindingKey?,bindingKind:principal|resource|permission|configuration|value,authorizedBy?:[guard keys],complete?:boolean}. Only binding nodes need bindingKey/bindingKind. Reject is terminating deny, effect is protected allow. after is explicit execution precedence, never array order. Each terminal represents one proposed path, complete only when all relevant entry/upstream/binding/control/effect dependencies have actually been examined. Related alternative outcomes use distinct pathKeys matching final branch IDs. condition is node reachability, NOT the proposition that a guard passes. Shared entry/binding nodes can precede multiple paths.
Use different typed identity keys for different objects even if labels/IDs match. authorizedBy asserts that a particular guard controls THIS effect on the same principal/resource; omit the assertion if no such linkage is established, and explain source-visible missing control rather than inventing a guard. Do not assume a checked input object also authorizes an output object.
Predicates support only {op:eq|neq,left:{binding:name}|{literal:scalar},right:value}, {op:is-null,value}, {op:all|any,args:[predicates]}, {op:not,arg:predicate}; scalar is string/number/boolean/null. Max depth12/nodes64. No target code, arbitrary operator or natural text is evaluated. Known bindings are only explicit USER premises: {questionId,key,value,origin:user,text:<exact span of current request/premise>}. This mapping is a model interpretation, not source truth; unspecified values stay unknown, distinct from null. Represent source outcomes with rules/conditions, do not invent user binding values from source.
Dependencies: {key,questionId,pathKey,from:<accepted source rule key>,symbol:<name appearing in cited source>,kind:principal-binding|resource-binding|control|effect|exception,decisive:boolean,evidenceIds:[source reference IDs],reason,condition?,after?:[preceding control keys],parent?:dependency key,pathHint?:exact indexed path,candidateId?:shown candidate id}. Host uses a lexical location index, not a semantic call graph. Ambiguous candidates require an explicit pathHint/candidateId revision; missing/outside/dynamic facts stay local gaps. Place a dependency after a reject only if source order actually makes it unreachable. After an automatic read, incorporate the returned original evidence into a linked rule before calling a decisive dependency checked.
Policy mappings are separate candidates: {key,questionId,pathKey,expected:allow|deny,origin:policy,text:<exact policy span>,location:<current independent location>,condition?}. Map only the supplied policy, do not derive it from implementation. Each live path needs a mapping for a determined policy assessment; incomplete mappings remain undetermined while behavior is deliverable. Formal policy mapping is still unreviewed.
Same-key duplicate is idempotent. To correct a conflicting accepted proposal, supply revisionOf:<host-returned digest> and revisionReason; no silent overwrite. Keep gaps local; one irrelevant relationship does not invalidate other questions. Host feedback is formal computation on proposed rules, not a source-semantic or deployment proof. At most64 nodes/question and16 paths/question; overflow remains a named gap.

Submit authorization_check_result({result}) with {schemaVersion:"authorization-inquiry-result/v1",questions:[{questionId,behavior:{disposition:allow|deny|conditional|unknown,explanation},branches:[{id,condition,disposition,explanation,evidenceIds}],evidenceIds,missing:[{kind:source-gap|premise-unspecified|deployment-unverified|dependency-out-of-scope,detail,nextRead?}],policyAssessment?:{status:satisfied|violated|undetermined,explanation}}],observations:[],scope}. Conformance requires policyAssessment; behavior forbids it. Branch id matches pathKey. unknown identifies a decisive gap. After one diagnostic repair at most, answer in the original skill prose format.

Runtime: existing SkVM plus Bun dependencies. Ordinary usage: skvm run --skill=SKILL.md --prompt=<current-task> --authorization-scope=<input.json> --authorization-domain-tools --authorization-strategy=domain-evidence-v1 --authorization-trace=<new-file> --model=<provider/model>. This extension does not perform target execution, deployment validation, patching or a whole audit.

rules.claim: The document notes action is an endpoint for GET and POST and uses PaperlessNotePermissions.
At the endpoint permission layer, GET requires the listed global model permissions documents.view_note and documents.view_document.
The addressed document is loaded by pk and its owner relation is selected; the document is the object passed to the owner-aware permission check.

On the GET branch, serialized notes for the addressed document are returned.
The document notes action is an endpoint for POST and uses PaperlessNotePermissions.
At the endpoint permission layer, POST requires documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document.
The addressed document is loaded by pk and its owner relation is selected; the document is the object passed to the owner-aware permission check.
Before the POST branch, the action calls has_perms_owner_aware for view_document on the addressed document and returns 403 if it fails.

rules.claim: has_perms_owner_aware returns true when the addressed document is unowned, owned by the caller, or the caller has the requested object permission.
After the endpoint model-permission control passes, GET returns the addressed document's serialized notes when the owner-aware check passes, including its owner and unowned alternatives.
For both view_document and change_document calls, has_perms_owner_aware returns true when the addressed document is unowned, owned by the caller, or the caller has the requested object permission.
After the endpoint model-permission control passes, POST creates a note on the addressed document when both owner-aware calls pass; ownership or no owner makes both pass without object grants.

behavior.explanation: GET is first gated by PaperlessNotePermissions: the caller must be authenticated and hold global documents.view_note plus documents.view_document model permissions. The action then loads the document selected by pk and applies has_perms_owner_aware(user, "view_document", doc). That object check passes if the document is unowned, owned by the caller, or the caller has the object-level view_document permission. If it passes, the endpoint returns that document's serialized notes.

branches.condition: The caller is absent/unauthenticated or lacks either global documents.view_note or global documents.view_document.
branches.explanation: PaperlessNotePermissions rejects the request before the action effect.

branches.condition: The endpoint model-permission gate passes, and the addressed document is owned by the caller or has no owner; no object grant is assumed.
branches.explanation: has_perms_owner_aware treats caller ownership and no owner as sufficient, and GET then returns the notes.

branches.condition: The endpoint model-permission gate passes, the addressed document is owned by someone else, and the caller has view_document on that document.
branches.explanation: The owner-aware check accepts the object grant and GET returns the notes.

branches.condition: The endpoint model-permission gate passes, the addressed document is owned by someone else, and the caller lacks view_document on that document.
branches.explanation: The owner-aware check fails and the action returns Forbidden.

missing.detail: The addressed document's owner relation is unspecified.
The caller's global model permissions and object-level view_document grant are unspecified.

policyAssessment.explanation: The policy requires an object-level view_document grant and says ownership is not a substitute. Source permits GET for caller-owned and unowned documents without that object grant, provided the separate endpoint model-permission gate passes. The other-owner branch with an object view_document grant conforms, while the missing-grant other-owner branch is denied.

behavior.explanation: POST is first gated by PaperlessNotePermissions: the authenticated caller must hold global documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document model permissions. The action loads the document selected by pk, applies an owner-aware view_document check, then an owner-aware change_document check. Each owner-aware check passes for an unowned document, caller ownership, or the corresponding object grant. If both pass, Note.objects.create writes a note linked to that same document and to request.user.

branches.condition: The caller is absent/unauthenticated or lacks any required global documents.add_note, documents.view_document, or documents.change_document permission.
branches.explanation: PaperlessNotePermissions rejects the request before note creation.

branches.condition: The endpoint model-permission gate passes, and the addressed document is owned by the caller or has no owner; no object grants are assumed.
branches.explanation: Both owner-aware checks pass through the owner/no-owner alternatives, after which a note is created on the addressed document.

branches.condition: The endpoint model-permission gate passes, the document is owned by someone else, and the caller has both view_document and change_document on that document.
branches.explanation: Both object checks pass and the note is created on the same addressed document.

branches.condition: The endpoint gate passes, the document is owned by someone else, and the caller lacks view_document on that document.
branches.explanation: The initial owner-aware view check returns Forbidden before the change check and creation.

branches.condition: The endpoint gate passes, the document is owned by someone else, the caller has view_document, but lacks change_document on that document.
branches.explanation: The view check passes, but the subsequent owner-aware change check returns Forbidden before creation.

missing.detail: The addressed document's owner relation is unspecified.
The caller's global model permissions and object-level view_document/change_document grants are unspecified.

policyAssessment.explanation: The policy requires change_document on the addressed document and rejects ownership as a substitute. Source permits POST for caller-owned and unowned documents without an object-level change_document grant (and without an object-level view_document grant), provided the endpoint's global model-permission gate passes. For a document owned by someone else, source requires both object view_document and change_document; that is stricter than the supplied creation policy but includes its required change_document grant.

behavior.explanation: GET requires the endpoint gate and then an owner-aware view_document check on the document selected by pk. The endpoint gate requires authentication plus global documents.view_note and documents.view_document. The object check accepts an unowned document, caller ownership, or an object-level view_document grant; successful GET returns that document's notes.

branches.condition: The endpoint gate passes and the owner-aware view_document check passes through an object grant on the addressed document.
branches.explanation: The action returns notes serialized from the same document loaded by pk.

branches.condition: The endpoint gate passes and the addressed document is caller-owned or unowned, with no object grant supplied.
branches.explanation: Ownership or no owner satisfies has_perms_owner_aware, so GET returns the notes.

policyAssessment.explanation: The object-grant branch conforms, but source also allows caller-owned and unowned documents without an object-level view_document grant. That conflicts with the policy's grant requirement and its statement that ownership is not a substitute.

behavior.explanation: POST requires authentication and global documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document at the endpoint. It then performs owner-aware view_document and change_document checks on the document selected by pk. Each accepts no owner, caller ownership, or its corresponding object grant. If both pass, the new note is linked to that same document.

branches.condition: The endpoint gate passes and the addressed document's owner-aware view_document and change_document checks pass through the corresponding object grants.
branches.explanation: The action creates a note on the same document loaded by pk.

branches.condition: The endpoint gate passes and the addressed document is caller-owned or unowned, with no object grants supplied.
branches.explanation: Ownership or no owner makes both owner-aware checks pass, after which the note is created.

branches.condition: The caller is unauthenticated or lacks any required global add_note, view_document, or change_document permission.
branches.explanation: PaperlessNotePermissions rejects before creation.

branches.explanation: The first owner-aware object check returns Forbidden.

branches.condition: The endpoint gate and object view check pass, but the other-owned document lacks object-level change_document for the caller.
branches.explanation: The subsequent change check returns Forbidden before creation.
